issues.label: DVPA jurisdiction and authority
issues.why: The court must confirm it has authority under the Domestic Violence Prevention Act to adjudicate the petition and issue or deny protective orders.

issues.label: Proper notice and service
issues.why: The court must ensure respondent received legally sufficient notice of the DVRO hearing and any continuances to satisfy due process.

issues.label: Adequacy of pleadings
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition alleges DVPA-qualifying abuse against protected persons sufficient to proceed to merits.

issues.label: Protected persons eligibility
issues.why: The court must confirm Wife and Child qualify as protected persons under DVPA given the parties’ relationship and child’s status.

issues.label: DVPA definition of abuse
issues.why: The court must apply the statutory definition of abuse (including coercive control, threats, harassment, and physical injury) to the facts.

issues.label: Burden of proof standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct DVPA standard (preponderance of evidence) for issuing a restraining order.

issues.label: Future harm necessity standard
issues.why: The court must decide whether issuance requires a reasonable apprehension/probability of future abuse and apply the correct legal test.

issues.label: Past abuse relevance
issues.why: The court must decide how past acts—especially in Nigeria years earlier—bear on current need for protection under DVPA.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must make credibility findings on conflicting accounts, including admissions of prior false statements to CWS.

issues.label: Evidentiary rulings correctness
issues.why: The court must ensure evidence was admitted/excluded under applicable rules (hearsay exceptions, authentication, relevance, prejudice).

issues.label: Audio recording foundation
issues.why: The court must confirm proper authentication, translation/understanding, completeness, and audibility for the Igbo/English recording.

issues.label: Translation and interpreter needs
issues.why: The court must ensure meaningful comprehension of non-English portions through interpreter/translation to preserve due process.

issues.label: Child abuse evidence treatment
issues.why: The court must address allegations of corporal punishment and threats toward Child as DVPA abuse and custody-related safety factors.

issues.label: Impact of CWS finding
issues.why: The court must determine the legal weight of an “unsubstantiated” CWS outcome and prior denials on DVPA findings.

issues.label: Effect of criminal protective order
issues.why: The court must consider existence and scope of any criminal protective order and how it interacts with DVPA relief.

issues.label: DVRO custody and visitation
issues.why: If DVRO relief is considered, the court must address custody/visitation orders, supervision, and DV presumption/safety terms.

issues.label: DV custody presumption
issues.why: The court must consider Family Code section 3044 presumption against custody to a perpetrator if DV is found within 5 years.

issues.label: Move-out and stay-away standards
issues.why: The court must apply statutory requirements for exclusive possession and stay-away distances if ordering such relief.

issues.label: Firearms relinquishment
issues.why: If a DVRO issues, the court must address mandatory firearm prohibitions and relinquishment procedures.

issues.label: Duration and scope of orders
issues.why: The court must set legally permissible duration (up to 5 years) and tailor terms to prevent abuse without overbreadth.

issues.label: Attorney fees and costs
issues.why: The court must consider statutory authority for fee-shifting/costs in DVPA proceedings where requested and supported.

issues.label: Continuance discretion limits
issues.why: The court must apply DVPA policies favoring merits determinations and ensure continuances/extensions were handled within statutory bounds.

issues.label: Trial time limits fairness
issues.why: The court must ensure time limits did not deprive either party of a meaningful opportunity to present evidence and cross-examine.

issues.label: Right to be heard
issues.why: The court must provide both sides a full and fair evidentiary hearing before denying or terminating DVPA protection.

issues.label: Improper dismissal as sanction
issues.why: The court must determine whether dismissal for exceeding time estimates functioned as an impermissible sanction without statutory basis.

issues.label: CCP 533 applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether Code of Civil Procedure section 533 applies to DVPA temporary orders and/or pending DVRO actions.

issues.label: CCP 533 procedural requirements
issues.why: If CCP 533 applies, the court must ensure proper motion procedure, notice, and evidentiary showing to modify/dissolve.

issues.label: Authority to dismiss petition
issues.why: The court must determine whether it had legal authority to dismiss the entire DVRO petition mid-hearing rather than decide merits.

issues.label: Distinguish dissolve vs dismiss
issues.why: The court must separate dissolving a temporary restraining order from adjudicating the requested permanent DVRO on the merits.

issues.label: Standard for dissolving DVTRO
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard for dissolving a temporary DVPA order pending adjudication, not a discretionary “cooling-off” test.

issues.label: Reliance on respondent promise
issues.why: The court must decide whether respondent’s voluntary assurances can legally substitute for DVPA findings and protective relief.

issues.label: Consideration of statutory factors
issues.why: The court must consider DVPA factors (history of abuse, threats, harm, disturbance of peace, coercive control) before denying relief.

issues.label: Due process in court questioning
issues.why: The court must ensure its limited direct examination of Husband did not improperly curtail examination by counsel or shift burdens.

issues.label: Incomplete evidentiary record
issues.why: The court must address whether ruling without allowing completion of testimony (including abuse denials) was legally permissible.

issues.label: Court reporter mishap impact
issues.why: The court must decide whether delayed reporting and responsibility dispute justifies any remedy and whether prejudice occurred.

issues.label: Sanction authority for delay
issues.why: The court must determine what sanctions/remedies are authorized for attorney scheduling/reporting failures short of dismissal of DVPA claims.

issues.label: Judicial bias/appearance concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether comments about attorney conduct/time created an appearance of prejudgment affecting fairness.

issues.label: Findings statement sufficiency
issues.why: The court must make legally sufficient findings on DVPA criteria when denying/dismissing, not solely procedural reasons.

issues.label: Record of rulings on objections
issues.why: The court must ensure evidentiary objections and rulings are adequately recorded for review and did not skew fact-finding.

issues.label: Immigration-related threats relevance
issues.why: The court must treat deportation threats and control as potential coercive control/disturbing the peace under DVPA.

issues.label: Financial control as abuse
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether alleged financial restrictions constitute DVPA abuse/coercive control even absent physical violence.

issues.label: Child presence during violence
issues.why: The court must consider child exposure to DV as a safety factor for both DVPA relief and custody/visitation terms.

issues.label: Safety at exchanges
issues.why: If orders are denied or dissolved, the court must consider protective terms for child exchanges to prevent conflict or harm.

issues.label: Without-prejudice effect
issues.why: The court must determine the legal consequences of dissolving/dismissing without prejudice on future filings and interim protections.

issues.label: Interaction with supervised visitation
issues.why: The court must address what happens to existing supervised visitation orders when the DVRO action is dismissed.

issues.label: Temporary orders pending trial
issues.why: The court must ensure interim custody/visitation and protective orders are properly maintained or terminated consistent with statutes.

issues.label: Local rules/time estimate enforcement
issues.why: The court must assess whether enforcing time estimates as hard caps complied with statewide rules and did not conflict with DVPA policies.

issues.label: Equitable considerations relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether costs, duration under TRO, and compliance are legally relevant to DVPA relief decisions.

issues.label: Mootness and case posture
issues.why: The court must consider whether dissolving the DVTRO mooted any issues or whether the petition still required adjudication.

issues.label: Appellate standard implications
issues.why: The court must recognize which decisions are discretionary vs legal error (e.g., statutory interpretation, due process) to decide correctly.
